newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka steps up security ahead of poll.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka steps up security ahead of poll.

text.p: Security was stepped up in Sri Lanka on Wednesday ahead of forthcoming local government polls after campaigning ended at midnight, police and officials said.
Newspapers said curfews were likely to be imposed in some areas and in the capital Colombo after polling ended on Friday to avoid post-election violence.
The independent Midweek Mirror quoted an unidentified Defence Ministry official as saying the curfew would be enforced soon after the voting was over.
But Colombo police chief D.M. Dissanayake told Reuters that a curfew was not on the cards.
"As of now, there doesn't seem to be a need for a curfew. But we will have to wait and see," he said.
Dissanayake said police have been instructed to crack down on those who conduct any campaign activity after the deadline.
"We are going to launch tough security measures to stop unruly elements from taking control. We are ready for any eventuality," he said.
Some 30,000 policemen will be deployed at polling stations across the country on election day.

The campaign has been marred by violence, beginning with the killing last month of a young legislator of the ruling People's Alliance (PA) during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and those from the main opposition United National Party (UNP).

The Centre for Monitoring Election Violence, an independent monitoring group, said 130 incidents of poll-related violence were reported on Tuesday, bringing to more than 1,800 the total number of incidents reported since nominations for the election closed on February 12.
The polls are the first political test for the PA government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga.

Nearly 20,000 candidates from 12 political parties and 132 independent groups are contesting 228 councils in Friday's poll throughout the country except the northern and eastern provinces where government forces are battling separatist Tamil rebels.
Seats for councils in 12 cities, 31 towns and 195 villages are being contested. The size of the councils range from nine seats in remote villages to 53 in Colombo.
